value.lineage: README: 'Version 2' of 'its predecessor (AI Scientist-v1)' at https://github.com/SakanaAI/AI-Scientist; 'The tree search component implemented within the ai_scientist directory is built on top of the AIDE project' (https://github.com/WecoAI/aideml); code still prints 'AIDE is working on experiment' and serialize.py docstring says 'Deserialize JSON to AIDE dataclasses'. Companion repo SakanaAI/AI-Scientist-ICLR2025-Workshop-Experiment linked from README. || main loop (reader, from the code): AgentManager.run iterates four fixed main stages (initial_implementation -> baseline_tuning -> creative_research -> ablation_studies), and within each sub-stage repeatedly calls ParallelAgent.step, which selects num_workers tree nodes (new drafts until num_drafts roots exist, random buggy leaves to debug with probability debug_prob, otherwise the LLM-judged best good node to improve, or the fixed best stage-1/3 node for hyperparameter/ablation stages), has worker processes ask an LLM for plan+code, execute it via Interpreter with a timeout, parse metrics and VLM plot feedback into a Node, appends the Nodes to the stage Journal, and ends the stage when max_iterations is reached or an LLM judges the stage goals met, then runs multi-seed evaluation and plot aggregation on the best node before seeding the next stage with it.

HUMAN_PROBLEM.value: A generalized end-to-end agentic system that autonomously generates hypotheses, runs experiments, analyzes data and writes scientific manuscripts, and that 'has generated the first workshop paper written entirely by AI and accepted through peer review' (README).

value.built_to: A generalized end-to-end agentic system that autonomously generates hypotheses, runs experiments, analyzes data and writes scientific manuscripts, and that 'has generated the first workshop paper written entirely by AI and accepted through peer review' (README).
value.pressure: The predecessor AI Scientist-v1 relied on human-authored templates; v2 'removes reliance on human-authored templates, generalizes across Machine Learning (ML) domains, and employs a progressive agentic tree search, guided by an experiment manager agent' (README), while noting v2 has lower success rates than v1 when a strong template exists.
value.success_means: Producing a completed paper PDF plus LLM/VLM review; README FAQ frames success as a per-run 'success rate' of completing experiments and generating a PDF, dependent on the foundation model and idea complexity, with a peer-review-accepted workshop paper as the headline result.

organs.mechanism: until the worker slots fill: draft while fewer than num_drafts (3) drafts exist; else with probability debug_prob (0.5) a buggy leaf within max_debug_depth (3); else (stages 1 and 3) the best node, falling back to good nodes by metric, one per tree; stages 2 and 4 expand the stage's best node
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: the first step drafts all 4 worker slots (more than num_drafts); <= max_debug_depth allows depth 4

organs.mechanism: unless restricted to the validation metric, the good nodes' ids and metrics are sent to an LLM (default gpt-4o at temperature 0.3) that names the best; on failure, the metric argmax
is_buggy = the reviewer's is_bug or an exception; failed or invalid metric parsing also marks it buggy; good nodes additionally need a vision model to accept the plots
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: a node that is not buggy but fails the plot check (or has none) is neither good nor buggy and is never selected again
